```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2026_PF06804103"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2026_PF06804103"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70261> (open access, PMC13274674)

Li 2026 developed three longitudinal models for PF-06804103, a site-specific
anti-HER2 antibody-drug conjugate, from the phase 1 study NCT03284723: a
two-compartment population PK model (Table 1), a repeated time-to-event (RTTE)
model for grade >= 2 peripheral neuropathy (PN) (Table 2), and a tumor-dynamics
model for the sum of longest diameters (Table 3). The PD models were fitted on
the individual PK estimates and the three were then integrated into one
adaptive-dosing trial simulation in which each PN event delays and reduces the
next dose, which in turn changes the exposure that drives later PN events and
tumor shrinkage. The authors published the NONMEM simulation code for the
integrated model (Supporting Information S1) and the PD equations (S2); this
package model reproduces that integrated model.

# Population

95 adults with HER2-expressing (HER2-positive or HER2-low) breast or gastric
cancer received PF-06804103 0.15-5 mg/kg as an IV infusion on Day 1 of every
3-week cycle. They contributed 1508 PK records, 35 grade >= 2 PN events and
335 tumor-size measurements. Li 2026 does not tabulate the baseline
demographics; the authors' code normalises body weight to 63.45 kg and the log
of the baseline sum of longest diameters to 3.98 (53.5 mm), which are taken
here as the analysis medians.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Li_2026_PF06804103")()$population)
```

# Virtual cohort

The paper simulated its 95 participants with their individual PK estimates and
covariates, which are not public. The virtual cohort below uses 150 subjects
with body weight log-normal around 63.45 kg (CV about 20%, 40-120 kg), 80%
female (breast and gastric cancer; the sex split is not reported) and baseline
sum of longest diameters log-normal around 53.5 mm (10-250 mm). Random effects
are drawn in base R from the model's omega matrix so that the cohort, and the
PN event thresholds, are identical on every machine; the same 150 subjects are
used for every regimen, so the regimen contrasts are paired.

```{r cohort}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2026_PF06804103"))
omega <- mod$omega

set.seed(20261113)
n_sub <- 150
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_sub, log(63.45), 0.2), 40), 120),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.8),
  TUM_SLD = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_sub, log(53.5), 0.6), 10), 250)
)
eta <- matrix(rnorm(n_sub * nrow(omega)), n_sub) %*% chol(omega)
colnames(eta) <- rownames(omega)
cohort <- bind_cols(cohort, as_tibble(eta))

# Exp(1) thresholds for the first three PN events: an event occurs when the
# cumulative hazard accrued since the previous event exceeds the threshold,
# which is the same rule as the authors' survival-vs-uniform comparison.
pn_threshold <- matrix(rexp(n_sub * 3), n_sub)

summary(cohort[, c("WT", "SEXF", "TUM_SLD")])
```

# Cycle-1 pharmacokinetics

Each starting dose is a 1-h IV infusion (the infusion rate in the authors'
simulation dataset). Figure 2 of Li 2026 shows individual peak concentrations
of roughly 45-55 ug/mL after 3-4 mg/kg.

```{r cycle1}
make_obs <- function(times, cohort, group) {
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = times) |>
    left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
    mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L, treatment = group)
}

make_dose <- function(dose_tbl, cohort, group) {
  dose_tbl |>
    left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
    mutate(amt = mgkg * WT, rate = amt, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
           dvid = NA_integer_, treatment = group) |>
    select(-mgkg)
}

c1_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 1), seq(24, 504, by = 12))))
c1_events <- bind_rows(lapply(c(3, 3.5, 4), function(d) {
  grp <- paste(d, "mg/kg")
  bind_rows(
    make_dose(tibble(id = cohort$id, time = 0, mgkg = d), cohort, grp),
    make_obs(c1_times, cohort, grp)
  ) |> mutate(id = id + 1000L * match(d, c(3, 3.5, 4)))
})) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

c1_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = c1_events, omega = NA, sigma = NA,
                          useLinCmt = FALSE, keep = "treatment",
                          returnType = "data.frame")

c1_sim |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, med, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (day)", y = "PF-06804103 (ug/mL)",
       colour = "Starting dose", fill = "Starting dose",
       caption = "Median and 90% interval of the virtual cohort, cycle 1.")
```

## PKNCA

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- c1_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

dose_df <- c1_events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, duration = 1)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 504, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        auclast = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Starting dose" = treatment,
    "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-504 (ug*h/mL)" = auclast,
    "AUC0-inf (ug*h/mL)" = aucinf.obs,
    "t1/2 (h)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated cycle-1 NCA (medians of the virtual cohort).")
```

Li 2026 reports no NCA, so the check is internal: for a linear model, AUC from
zero to infinity must equal dose / CL for every subject. Both sides use the same
drawn parameters, so the bound only has to absorb the trapezoidal and
extrapolation error. The simulated Cmax is also checked against the 45-55
ug/mL peaks of Figure 2.

```{r pknca-check}
cl_ind <- exp(log(0.03089) + cohort$etalcl)
auc_chk <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  left_join(dose_df |> select(id, treatment, amt), by = c("id", "treatment")) |>
  mutate(expected = amt / cl_ind[id %% 1000L],
         pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / expected - 1))
cmax_4 <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax", treatment == "4 mg/kg") |>
  pull(PPORRES)

stopifnot(
  abs(median(auc_chk$pct_diff)) < 2,
  quantile(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 5,
  median(cmax_4) > 40, median(cmax_4) < 70
)
summary(auc_chk$pct_diff)
```

# Adaptive-dosing simulation

The dose-modification rules follow the Methods and the authors' code. Doses are
given every 504 h (3 weeks) up to 6048 h. At each grade >= 2 PN event the next
scheduled dose is delayed by 2 weeks (1 week in the fourth regimen) and the dose
drops one level; a PN event at the lowest level (2 mg/kg) ends treatment. The
four regimens are 4 -> 3 -> 2 mg/kg, 3.5 -> 2.75 -> 2 mg/kg, 3 -> 2 mg/kg, and
3 -> 2 mg/kg with the 1-week delay.

rxode2 cannot change a dosing history from inside the ODE the way the NONMEM
`COM()` variables do, so the vignette re-solves each subject with the dosing
history implied by its events so far. Each pass finds every subject's next PN
event on a daily grid, rewrites the doses after it, and re-solves. Doses before
an event never change, so earlier events stay where they were.

```{r adaptive-helpers}
horizon <- 6048
grid <- seq(0, horizon, by = 24)

adaptive_events <- function(doses, cohort, group) {
  bind_rows(make_dose(doses, cohort, group), make_obs(grid, cohort, group)) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

solve_adaptive <- function(doses, cohort, group) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = adaptive_events(doses, cohort, group),
                  omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE,
                  returnType = "data.frame")
}

# First grid time after t_prev at which the cumulative hazard accrued since
# t_prev reaches the subject's threshold; NA if none before the horizon.
next_event_time <- function(sim, t_prev, threshold) {
  sim |>
    select(id, time, cumhaz) |>
    filter(!is.na(t_prev[id]), time >= t_prev[id]) |>
    group_by(id) |>
    mutate(gain = cumhaz - first(cumhaz)) |>
    summarise(t_event = time[which(gain >= threshold[first(id)])[1]], .groups = "drop")
}

# Remove the doses at or after the event and, unless the subject is at the
# lowest level, restart the schedule at (next scheduled dose + delay).
modify_doses <- function(doses, i, t_event, next_level, delay) {
  mine <- doses$id == i
  upcoming <- doses$time[mine & doses$time >= t_event]
  doses <- doses[!(mine & doses$time >= t_event), ]
  if (!is.na(next_level) && length(upcoming) > 0) {
    t1 <- min(upcoming) + delay
    if (t1 <= horizon - 1) {
      doses <- bind_rows(doses, tibble(id = i, time = seq(t1, horizon - 1, by = 504),
                                       mgkg = next_level))
    }
  }
  doses
}

run_regimen <- function(reg, cohort, pn_threshold) {
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = seq(0, horizon - 1, by = 504)) |>
    mutate(mgkg = reg$levels[1])
  ev_t <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(cohort), length(reg$levels))
  for (k in seq_along(reg$levels)) {
    sim <- solve_adaptive(doses, cohort, reg$name)
    t_prev <- if (k == 1) rep(0, nrow(cohort)) else ev_t[, k - 1]
    hit <- next_event_time(sim, t_prev, pn_threshold[, k]) |> filter(!is.na(t_event))
    if (nrow(hit) == 0) break
    ev_t[hit$id, k] <- hit$t_event
    for (j in seq_len(nrow(hit))) {
      doses <- modify_doses(doses, hit$id[j], hit$t_event[j],
                            reg$levels[k + 1], reg$delay)
    }
  }
  sim <- solve_adaptive(doses, cohort, reg$name)
  list(sim = mutate(sim, regimen = reg$name), ev_t = ev_t,
       doses = mutate(doses, regimen = reg$name))
}
```

```{r adaptive-run}
regimens <- list(
  list(name = "3 mg/kg", levels = c(3, 2), delay = 336),
  list(name = "3 mg/kg (1-week delay)", levels = c(3, 2), delay = 168),
  list(name = "3.5 mg/kg", levels = c(3.5, 2.75, 2), delay = 336),
  list(name = "4 mg/kg", levels = c(4, 3, 2), delay = 336)
)
adaptive <- lapply(regimens, run_regimen, cohort = cohort, pn_threshold = pn_threshold)
names(adaptive) <- vapply(regimens, `[[`, "", "name")
```

## Tumor response and study status

Tumor size is read weekly, as in the authors' simulation dataset. A subject
leaves the study at the first week with tumor size >= 120% of its nadir
(progression) or after the PN event that ends treatment. An objective response
is a decrease of >= 30% from baseline at any on-study week up to the cut-off.
The simulated tumor size is the individual prediction, without residual error.

```{r tumor-status}
tumor_status <- function(res, n_levels) {
  t_disc <- res$ev_t[, n_levels]
  res$sim |>
    filter(time %% 168 == 0) |>
    group_by(id) |>
    arrange(time, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    mutate(
      pchg = 100 * (tumor_size / first(tumor_size) - 1),
      prior_nadir = lag(cummin(tumor_size), default = first(tumor_size)),
      progressed = cumsum(tumor_size >= 1.2 * prior_nadir) > 0,
      discontinued = !is.na(t_disc[id]) & time > t_disc[id],
      on_study = !progressed & !discontinued
    ) |>
    ungroup()
}

tumor <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(regimens), function(r) {
  tumor_status(adaptive[[r]], length(regimens[[r]]$levels))
}))
```

## Comparison with Table 4

```{r table4}
summarise_regimen <- function(r, cutoff) {
  ev_t <- adaptive[[r]]$ev_t
  n_lev <- length(regimens[[r]]$levels)
  orr <- tumor |>
    filter(regimen == regimens[[r]]$name, time <= cutoff, on_study) |>
    group_by(id) |>
    summarise(resp = any(pchg <= -30), .groups = "drop")
  tibble(
    regimen = regimens[[r]]$name,
    cycle = if (cutoff == 2016) "Cycle 5" else "Cycle 9",
    ORR = 100 * sum(orr$resp) / n_sub,
    `Dose reduction >= 1` = 100 * mean(!is.na(ev_t[, 1]) & ev_t[, 1] <= cutoff),
    Discontinuation = 100 * mean(!is.na(ev_t[, n_lev]) & ev_t[, n_lev] <= cutoff)
  )
}

sim_t4 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(regimens), function(r) {
  bind_rows(summarise_regimen(r, 2016), summarise_regimen(r, 4032))
})) |>
  pivot_longer(c(ORR, `Dose reduction >= 1`, Discontinuation),
               names_to = "endpoint", values_to = "simulated")

pub_t4 <- tribble(
  ~endpoint, ~regimen, ~cycle, ~published,
  "ORR", "3 mg/kg", "Cycle 5", 38,
  "ORR", "3 mg/kg", "Cycle 9", 40,
  "ORR", "3 mg/kg (1-week delay)", "Cycle 5", 39,
  "ORR", "3 mg/kg (1-week delay)", "Cycle 9", 41,
  "ORR", "3.5 mg/kg", "Cycle 5", 44,
  "ORR", "3.5 mg/kg", "Cycle 9", 46,
  "ORR", "4 mg/kg", "Cycle 5", 49,
  "ORR", "4 mg/kg", "Cycle 9", 50,
  "Dose reduction >= 1", "3 mg/kg", "Cycle 5", 43,
  "Dose reduction >= 1", "3 mg/kg", "Cycle 9", 64,
  "Dose reduction >= 1", "3 mg/kg (1-week delay)", "Cycle 5", 42,
  "Dose reduction >= 1", "3 mg/kg (1-week delay)", "Cycle 9", 64,
  "Dose reduction >= 1", "3.5 mg/kg", "Cycle 5", 44,
  "Dose reduction >= 1", "3.5 mg/kg", "Cycle 9", 67,
  "Dose reduction >= 1", "4 mg/kg", "Cycle 5", 47,
  "Dose reduction >= 1", "4 mg/kg", "Cycle 9", 69,
  "Discontinuation", "3 mg/kg", "Cycle 5", 10,
  "Discontinuation", "3 mg/kg", "Cycle 9", 27,
  "Discontinuation", "3 mg/kg (1-week delay)", "Cycle 5", 11,
  "Discontinuation", "3 mg/kg (1-week delay)", "Cycle 9", 27,
  "Discontinuation", "3.5 mg/kg", "Cycle 5", 2,
  "Discontinuation", "3.5 mg/kg", "Cycle 9", 9,
  "Discontinuation", "4 mg/kg", "Cycle 5", 2,
  "Discontinuation", "4 mg/kg", "Cycle 9", 10
)

t4 <- left_join(pub_t4, sim_t4, by = c("endpoint", "regimen", "cycle")) |>
  mutate(simulated = round(simulated), difference = simulated - published)

t4 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Endpoint" = endpoint, "Starting dose" = regimen, "Cut-off" = cycle,
    "Li 2026 Table 4 (%)" = published, "Simulated (%)" = simulated,
    "Difference (points)" = difference
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Table 4 of Li 2026 (published values are medians over 500 simulated trials of the 95 study participants).")

stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(t4$simulated)),
  # Every cell within 12 percentage points of the published median. The
  # published 95% intervals are about +/- 10 points, and the virtual cohort
  # differs from the study participants.
  max(abs(t4$difference)) < 12,
  # The paper's conclusions: 4 mg/kg gives the highest ORR and the 3 mg/kg
  # regimens the highest discontinuation.
  with(sim_t4, simulated[endpoint == "ORR" & regimen == "4 mg/kg" & cycle == "Cycle 5"] -
    simulated[endpoint == "ORR" & regimen == "3 mg/kg" & cycle == "Cycle 5"]) > 3,
  with(sim_t4, simulated[endpoint == "Discontinuation" & regimen == "3 mg/kg" & cycle == "Cycle 9"] -
    simulated[endpoint == "Discontinuation" & regimen == "4 mg/kg" & cycle == "Cycle 9"]) > 8
)
```

The dose-reduction rate is the most direct test of the PK and RTTE models: it
depends only on the exposure before the first PN event. The simulated rates sit
2-7 points below the published medians in every regimen, inside the published
95% intervals; a consistent offset of this size is expected from a virtual
cohort whose body-weight and PK distributions differ from the 95 study
participants. The agreement also confirms that the hazard runs on the
concentration in ng/mL. With the concentration in ug/mL the first-event
probability by cycle 5 at 4 mg/kg falls to about 10%, against 47% in Table 4.

```{r figure2}
ex_id <- ex_id[1]
ex <- adaptive[["4 mg/kg"]]$sim |> filter(id == ex_id)

ggplot(ex, aes(time / 504 + 1)) +

  geom_vline(xintercept = ex_events[!is.na(ex_events)] / 504 + 1, colour = "red") +

       caption = "One simulated subject starting at 4 mg/kg; red lines mark grade >= 2 PN events (cf. Figure 2 of Li 2026).")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Concentration units of the PN hazard.** The hazard is driven by the
  concentration in ng/mL (1000 x `Cc`), while the tumor kill term uses ug/mL.
  Table 3 states the KD units in ug/mL; Table 2 gives no units for alpha. The
  authors' code computes one concentration (amount in mcg over volume in L,
  i.e. ng/mL, per its header) for both terms. Only ng/mL for the hazard
  reproduces the dose-reduction rates of Table 4 (above), and only ug/mL for the
  tumor term reproduces the tumor shrinkage of Figure 3, so the model uses each
  sub-model's own unit.
* **Central-volume covariates.** Table 1 lists 'ThetaMale-V1' = -0.3186 and
  'ThetaSex-BWT' = -0.6198 without the covariate equations. The Methods state
  that categorical covariates entered linearly and continuous ones as power
  functions, and the Results that body weight and sex were the two covariates on
  Vc, so the model uses `Vc = ThetaVc * (1 + ThetaMale * male) * (WT / 63.45)^ThetaBWT`
  and reads 'ThetaSex-BWT' as the body-weight exponent. No reference weight is
  printed for the PK model; 63.45 kg is the reference weight of the authors'
  tumor-model code for the same participants. The PK covariates do not appear
  in the authors' code, which used each participant's individual PK estimates.
* **Code values that differ from the tables.** The published simulation code
  carries slightly different values from Tables 2 and 3: log(KTR) -7.64 vs
  -7.47, log(alpha) -15 vs -15.2, log(gamma) -0.961 vs -0.959, KG exponents 5.37
  and 5.02 vs 5.097 and 4.536, and an alpha IIV variance of 0.278 vs 0.0205. The
  model uses the final estimates in the tables; the structure, the covariate
  reference values (63.45 kg, 3.98) and the log transform of baseline SLD come
  from the code.
* **Omitted bookkeeping state.** The code's effect-AUC compartment (`EFFAUC`,
  `DADT(6) = KTR * A(3)`) does not enter any equation and is not included.
* **Infusion duration.** Doses are 1-h infusions, as in the authors' simulation
  dataset (rate = amount); the paper does not state the duration.
* **Simulation harness.** The NONMEM code changes doses through `COM()`
  variables during integration; the vignette reaches the same dosing histories
  by re-solving after each event, detecting events on a daily grid. The tumor
  is read weekly as in the authors' dataset, progression is >= 20% above the
  nadir, and ORR counts responses among all simulated subjects.
* **Virtual cohort.** The paper simulated its 95 participants with their
  individual PK estimates. The virtual cohort draws PK random effects from
  Table 1 and assumes the covariate distributions given above (body weight,
  80% female, baseline SLD); the paper does not report them. The KG covariate
  exponents are large, so ORR is sensitive to these distributions.
